facts.statement: Fossils of Cimoliasaurus have been found in New Jersey, North Carolina, and Maryland.
facts.quote: Cimoliasaurus was a plesiosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of the eastern United States, with fossils known from New Jersey, North Carolina, and Maryland.

facts.statement: A tentative record of Cimoliasaurus exists from Maryland, where a vertebra was discovered by Colin McEwen in 1988.
facts.quote: There is also a tentative record from the Maastrichtian-aged Severn Formation in Maryland when in 1988, Colin McEwen discovered a vertebra of a Cimoliasaurus during a school field trip.

facts.statement: Cimoliasaurus grew to a length of 4 to 7 meters.
facts.quote: Llegó a medir de 4 a 7 metros de largo

facts.statement: Cimoliasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) in the eastern United States.
facts.quote: Cimoliasaurus was a plesiosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of the eastern United States

facts.statement: Cimoliasaurus is classified as a derived elasmosaurid, making the family Cimoliasauridae a junior synonym of Elasmosauridae.
facts.quote: Nowadays, Cimoliasaurus is now recognized as being a derived elasmosaurid, effectively making the family name Cimoliasauridae Delair, 1959 a junior synonym of Elasmosauridae.

facts.statement: The name Cimoliasaurus means "white chalk lizard" because the fossil deposits resemble the chalk of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: The name is derived from the Greek Κιμωλία kimolia, meaning "white chalk", and σαύρος sauros, meaning "lizard", in reference to the fact that the deposits in which it was found bear a superficial resemblance to the chalk deposits of the Western Interior Seaway.

facts.statement: The species Cimoliasaurus teplicensis is considered a nomen dubium.
The genus Cimoliasaurus has a time range from the Kimmeridgian to the Maastrichtian (154.8 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Maastrichtian (154.8 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species Cimoliasaurus magnus was named by Joseph Leidy in 1851 based on cervical vertebrae found in New Jersey.
rejected.quote: The name Cimoliasaurus magnus was coined by Joseph Leidy for ANSP 9235, one anterior and 12 posterior cervical vertebrae collected in Maastrichtian-aged greensand deposits of the New Egypt and Navesink Formations in Burlington County, New Jersey.
